subject: Notice of new subprocessors — DPA amendment steps & e-sign sequencing
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmecloud.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>, procurements@acmecloud.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: addition of new subprocessors and DPA amendment steps

Hi Diego —

We want to let Redwood know that Acme Cloud will be adding two subprocessors to our platform that process customer telemetry: CloudLogix, Inc. (US) and TelemetryOps GmbH (DE). I attached the full subprocessor CSV for your records and a proposed DPA amendment (v2) that reflects the change.

Operationally, our legal team will run a short e-sign amendment to the DPA via DocuSign. Proposal is:
- Notification effective date: 2027-05-28 (today)
- 30-day general notice period from the effective date
- 14-day objection window once you acknowledge receipt (to keep timelines predictable)

If you intend to raise an objection, please provide it in writing during the 14-day window with the specific grounds and (if applicable) a remediation request. If no objection is received, we will proceed to execute the amendment and route DocuSign to Redwood's signatory.

Next steps we propose from our side: we will upload the DPA amendment to DocuSign and send a link to your procurement and legal contacts. Attaching the security profile for CloudLogix as requested previously.

Attached: acme_subprocessor_list_20270528.csv, proposed_dpa_amendment_v2.docx, acme-security-profile-CloudLogix.pdf

Thanks — happy to run a quick call if helpful.

—Sara
Sara Nguyen
Head of Legal Operations, Acme Cloud
S: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmecloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of new subprocessors and DPA amendment steps

Thanks, Sara — received and uploaded to our tracker. A few quick clarifications so we can respond internally and to your procurement team: 

1) Notice windows: your note mentions a 30-day notice with a 14-day objection window once we "acknowledge". Can you confirm whether the 30-day clock runs from 2027-05-28 regardless of acknowledgement, or whether acknowledgement triggers the 30-day clock? We need to align this with downstream customer commitments.

2) Objection process: please confirm what information you will provide to support evaluation (we typically need: vendor security summary, location of processing, data flow diagrams for telemetry, and whether subprocessor will have access to customer PII). The attached security profile for CloudLogix is helpful but we may need a short assessment matrix we can share with InfoSec.

3) DocuSign path: will the amendment require a signature from our Procurement/Legal? If so, please include a routing order and indicate whether the document will allow for redline acceptance or is presented as a final amendment. 

Cc'ing Laura (contracts) and Priyom (privacy/legal) to confirm sequencing from our side. I will consolidate and aim to get a formal Redwood response within 3 business days once we have the routing/clock confirmation.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Notice: addition of new subprocessors and DPA amendment steps

Forwarding Acme's notice. My quick take: we should accept the addition subject to two changes to their proposed sequencing:

- Make the 30-day effective notice run from the date of the initial notification (they proposed this, but Diego's point about acknowledgement matters for contractual notice to our customers). Suggest we agree to 30 days from notification but preserve a 14-calendar-day objection window (starts on our acknowledgement). That way the overall customer-facing notice remains predictable and we keep a short internal objection review period.

- We should not sign a 'final' amendment without the ability to incorporate a short redline clause that allows Redwood to require CloudLogix to:
  • provide completed SOC2 or equivalent evidence within 30 days of execution, and
  • accept a contractual data access limitation for telemetry (no PII unless explicitly agreed).

Priyom — can you draft a tight paragraph we can insert into their amendment that captures the objection mechanism and evidence requirement? Also include language to require they provide a 1-page vendor profile for TelemetryOps.

Attaching suggested redline outline for legal to paste into DocuSign if they permit partial redlines; if they don't, we'll request they accept the insertion before routing.

—Laura

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmecloud.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of new subprocessors and DPA amendment steps

Hi Sara — thanks for the notification and the materials. Acme's proposed sequencing mostly works for us; a couple of edits we need before we can sign: 

1) Notice & objection timing (redline language below):
"Acme will provide written notice to Customer and relevant Customer affiliates of the addition of any subprocessor ("Notice"). The Notice will be effective on the date sent to Customer. Customer will have fourteen (14) calendar days from Customer's acknowledgement of the Notice to submit a written objection setting forth specific, reasonable grounds why the proposed subprocessor's processing would not comply with the data protection obligations applicable to Customer. If Customer submits a timely objection, the parties will meet in good faith to attempt to resolve the objection. If not resolved within a further thirty (30) days, Customer may exercise available remedies under the DPA."

2) Evidence & access limitations: require CloudLogix to provide: completed security questionnaire, SOC2 report (or equivalent) within 30 days of execution, and a vendor profile. Insert clause limiting telemetry processors from accessing PII unless explicitly authorized.

3) DocuSign routing: we prefer a non-editable DocuSign for the base amendment plus a separate short redline addendum that can be attached and signed if needed. If Acme insists on single doc editing, we require trackable change acceptance or a signatory with authority to accept our inserted addendum.

Sara — if you can: (a) confirm the 30-day notice start is the date sent (fine), (b) send the DocuSign link with routing for Redwood Legal > Procurement > Authorized Signatory, and (c) attach CloudLogix SOC2 or a link to the evidence portal. 

I will prepare the exact insertion text and send it as a suggested addendum for DocuSign. If you prefer a call to walk through the process, I'm happy to do a short 20-minute slot this week.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
